**Stacked on #715** (grblHAL post, not merged yet): this branch is #715's head plus one commit, so the diff shows #715's files too until it merges. Only commit `feat(machines): Sienci AltMill ...` is this PR. Fork synced at v0.16.0 (via #715's base).

## What changed

Three built-in machines for Sienci's AltMill routers, which run grblHAL on the SLB-EXT controller. They post through the existing `grblhal.cps`; there is no AltMill post file.

- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `-4x4.mch` and `-4x8.mch`, registered in `posting::MACHINES` as "Sienci AltMill 2x4", "4x4" and "4x8".

- **`safe_retract: 0.0`.** The AltMill homes (`$22=79`: homing on, required at startup, machine origin 0 at home; Z homes up; soft limits on). So every tool change lifts `G53 G0 Z0`, then `T<n> M6` stands alone. gSender and ncSender take over on `T<n> M6` (manual change, RapidChange or Sienci ATC), so the post needs no ATC or manual mode and no rack list.
- **Figures** from Sienci's spec pages. The 4x4's travel (1260 x 1248 x 170 mm soft limits), axis rates and spindle range (1200-24000 rpm) are read from a 4x4's own `$$`. Every figure and its source is in `docs/decisions/728-altmill.md`.

## How tested

- New `altmill_machines.rs` (4 tests): each file's figures; the `G53 G0 Z0` lift before each `T<n> M6` and no G43/G43.1/G49; a spindle speed past 24000 refused; the 4x4 two-tool program locked byte-exact in mm and inch (`golden/nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool{,_inch}.nc`).
- Green on macOS: `altmill_machines`, `machine` (the library list now pins the three), `machine_library`, `machine_edit`, `conformance`, `grblhal_post`, `tormach_machines`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test altmill_machines -- -D warnings` is clean.

- No run on the machine yet. The owner has an AltMill 4x4 with an SLB-EXT, an 8-pocket RapidChange ATC and ncSender, and will report an air-cut of the 4x4 golden here.
- The 2x4 and 4x8 figures come from Sienci's pages only; an owner's `$$` would confirm them.
- Full workspace gate not run (disk-limited machine); the suites above are the ones that touch the machine registry and the grblHAL post.

title: docs(process): the camcraft-mcp skill's tool signatures match the server, with a drift test
body:
**Fixes #724.** The `camcraft-mcp` skill told agents argument names the server refuses, for 8 tools. This corrects them, brings the gap list current, and adds a test so the skill can't drift from `tools/list` silently again.

**Process change:** `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 4 -> 5. A suggested #681 line for the merging session:

> **PROCESS_VERSION 5** · PR #(this) · the `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool signatures now match the server (`post` takes `output`, `add_operation` takes `source`, `set_stock` takes `box {dx, dy, dz}` / `cylinder` / `from_model`, `set_operation_area` / `set_operation_geometry` take `operation`, `set_work_offset` takes `word`, `load_machine` takes `builtin` / `path` / `clear`, `add_tool` takes `catalog`), and its gap list is current. **Fork action:** pull the process files; an agent that learned the old names should use the new ones.

### What changed

- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the tool reference:** the 8 drifted entries now use the names the server publishes. The list is in #724.
- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, "Known Remaining Gaps":**
  - Moved to "shipped": pocket recognition (#35, `detect_pockets`), in-plane part axes (#557, `set_part_axes`), and the live GUI session (#183, #567, `--mcp-port` / `mcp --connect`). Also three-point alignment (#555, `lay_part_on_points`) and the fixture locate (#561, `locate_part`), which merged while this PR was open (3961e031).
  - `MoveModel` and `RepairModel` now point to their open PRs, #719 and #721.
  - Face-to-plane alignment (#330) is noted as GUI-only.
- **`crates/app/tests/mcp_skill_signatures.rs` (new), the drift alarm:** for every `` - `name { … }` `` signature in the skill, the tool must exist, each top-level documented key must be an `inputSchema` property, and each required argument must be documented.
  - A floor on how many signatures it finds (30; the skill has 34) keeps a format change from making it pass on nothing.
  - `the_key_reader_takes_top_level_keys_only` pins the small parser itself: quoted values and nested object fields aren't arguments.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`:** 4 -> 5.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/724-mcp-skill-signatures.md`.

No product code changes.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 47a7d0e7.

The other 2 of the 8 (`set_stock`, `add_tool`) were wrong in their prose, which the test doesn't read.

title: fix(app): verify's ok is false while an op's own warnings hold the post
body:
**Fixes #722.** `verify` said `"ok": true` for a program whose post was then refused by the ops' own warnings. So `camcraft-cli process <project>` (no `-o`) exited 0, "clean", for a job it couldn't post.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/script/api.rs`, `v_verify`:** behind `cam.verify`, `cam.check` and the MCP `verify` tool, and through them the CLI's exit code.
  - `ok` now also requires that no op in scope holds the post with its own cached warnings.
  - The rule is the post's own, in the new `holds_post`: a suppressed op is not in the program, and a warning counts exactly when `Warning::blocks_post()` is true. That is when `posting::stream_records` writes it as a `WARN` record, and any `WARN` record refuses the post. A Scallop or ProbeSearch note still doesn't count.
  - The report gains `held_by`: the labels of the ops in scope holding the post, empty when none.
- **`assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` and its template in `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`:** `VerifyReport` documents `ok` and the new `held_by` (the bindings drift test keeps the two equal).
- **`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`:** the `verify` tool's description says what `ok` and `held_by` mean.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/722-verify-ok-warnings.md`.

What stays the same: the program gate (`posting::verification_report`), the post's refusal text, and the findings list. Only the summary now agrees with them.

**Behaviour change, intended:** `camcraft-cli process <project>` without `-o` now exits 1 ("the job is not clean") for a job whose ops' warnings would refuse the post. Before, it exited 0.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_verify.rs`, new)

The fixture is a real collision. `EM-0400-2FL` is a Ø4 cutter with 12 mm of flute on a Ø6 shank, so contouring a 30 mm wall rubs the shank on the part below the flutes (84 `shank_hit` findings). A 10 mm wall stays inside the flutes and is clean.

- `verify_is_not_ok_while_an_ops_own_warnings_hold_the_post`: the 30 mm job has a fresh op and a passing gate, and every finding blocks the post. `ok` is `false`, `held_by` is `["C1"]` (the same answer for `verify {name: "C1"}`), and the post is still refused with "warning(s)".
- `a_contour_inside_the_flutes_still_verifies_ok_and_posts`: the 10 mm neighbour has no findings, `ok: true`, `held_by: []`, and the post writes.
- `the_cli_process_lane_exits_one_for_a_job_its_warnings_hold`: both jobs saved as projects and run through the real `camcraft-cli process`. The 30 mm job exits 1 with "not clean", the 10 mm job exits 0.

With `api.rs` put back to `main`, all three fail. The first fails at `a program the post refuses is not ok`, and the CLI test because the held job exits 0. The neighbour fails too, but only because `held_by` is a new key.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 43943371.

- **Quick gate plan** (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`), plus the other suites that read verify's `ok` (`mcp_setup`, `mcp_live`, `mcp_render`, `contour_arc_sim`, `wall_column_gouge`, `program_entry`), run by hand at `-j 4`. No failures, nothing ignored.
  - App lib: 103 passed.
  - Suites: `cli` 7, `contour_arc_sim` 1, `mcp` 13, `mcp_live` 10, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp_pockets` 3, `mcp_render` 5, `mcp_setup` 4, `mcp_verify` 3, `post_not_judged` 4, `program_entry` 9, `scripting` 18 (including the bindings drift test), `setup_mounts_post` 6, `wall_column_gouge` 3.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **The original report**, reproduced by hand on `main` f42d3788 with `camcraft-cli mcp` and `camcraft-cli process` (see #722).
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, the batch tier. The GUI is untouched: its status line reads `verification_report`, which this PR doesn't change.

Changelog: `verify` (and `camcraft-cli process` without `-o`) no longer reports a job as clean when an operation's own warnings would refuse the post; the report names those operations under `held_by` (#722)

Fixes #722

title: feat(app): an MCP repair_model tool welds and closes an imported mesh
body:
**Fixes #717.** Adds an MCP `repair_model` tool, so a headless session can close an imported mesh's open edges. Until now, only the Model page's Repair button could do that.

**Stacked on #719** (#716, `move_model`): both add to the new `crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs` and `crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`. This PR's own change is the last commit, b595b24e. Please merge #719 first; this PR will then merge `main` and show only its own diff.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`:** the `repair_model { name, weld_tol?, max_hole_edges? }` tool.
  - It builds the GUI's own `RepairModel` and runs it through the document History: one undo step that restores the exact previous facets.
  - The defaults are the Model page's, 0.001 mm and 256 edges (`RepairUi::default`), kept as named constants.
  - The reply carries every `RepairReport` count (vertices and triangles before and after, `welded`, `dropped`, `holes_filled`, `triangles_added`) and the command's one-line `summary`.
  - The repair runs at construction, so a refused repair never reaches the history. Every refusal is the command's own text: an unknown name, setup furniture, a negative tolerance, a budget under 3 edges, a repair refusal, and "nothing to repair". The tool itself only refuses a value of the wrong JSON type, by name.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/717-mcp-repair-model.md`.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`)

- `repair_model_fills_an_open_boxs_missing_face_in_one_undo_step`: an STL box with its top face left out has 10 facets. The repair reports 1 hole filled with 2 triangles (10 to 12), the defaults 0.001 and 256, and "filled 1 hole". Undo brings back the 10 facets and redo the 12. A second repair is refused with "nothing to repair".
- `repair_model_refuses_by_name_and_a_refusal_enters_no_history`: each case is refused by name: a closed box ("nothing to repair"), an unknown name, `weld_tol: -0.1`, `max_hole_edges: 2`, `max_hole_edges: 2.5`, a string tolerance, a missing name. Nothing changes, and the next `undo` still undoes the last import.

On `main` both fail at their first `repair_model` call, because the tool doesn't exist there.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on b595b24e.

- **Quick gate plan** (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 6`): no failures, nothing ignored.
  - App lib: 103 passed.
  - App suites: `contour_arc_sim` 1, `mcp` 13, `mcp_live` 10, `mcp_model` 5, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp_pockets` 3, `mcp_render` 5, `mcp_setup` 4, `wall_column_gouge` 3.
  - UI `models`: 4 passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, the batch tier. The existing command-level suite `repair_model` isn't in the plan either, because `RepairModel` is unchanged. `camcraft-cli mcp` over stdio wasn't tried; the tests drive the same `Server::handle` in-process.

With this PR, the `camcraft-mcp` skill's gap 3 (`RepairModel`) is done too. The skill is left alone for the same reason given in #719: editing it is a process change, with a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump.

title: feat(app): an MCP move_model tool places and turns an imported part
body:
**Fixes #716.** Adds an MCP `move_model` tool, so a headless session can place and turn an imported part. Until now, only the GUI's model move could do that.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs` (new):** the `move_model { name, position: [x, y, z], rotation?: [x, y, z, w] }` tool.
  - It builds the GUI's own `MoveModel` command and runs it through the document History, so the move is one undo step.
  - An omitted rotation keeps the part's current one, so lifting a part doesn't untwist it. A non-unit quaternion is normalized by the command, as for fixtures.
  - The reply holds the part's new placement and a `stock` list: each stock that moved with the part (stock made from it, or a one-part document's stock), with its new placement.
  - Every refusal is `MoveModel`'s own text, returned as a tool error: a fixture, a work offset, the machine table, an unknown name, a rotation that isn't a quaternion. A short or missing `position` is named too.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs`:** a new read-only accessor, `MoveModel::following_stock()`. It names the stock the move carries, so the tool can report it.
- **`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `mod.rs`:** the new module's rows are registered after the align tools.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/716-mcp-move-model.md`.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`, new)

- `a_moved_part_carries_a_one_part_documents_stock_and_one_undo_puts_both_back`: `tools/list` shows the tool with `name` and `position` required. Dropping a 20 x 10 x 4 box 4 mm moves its bounds to z -4..0. The box stock's bounds move by the same 4 mm and the reply lists that stock. Undo and redo restore and replay both bounds exactly.
- `a_quarter_turn_swaps_x_and_y_and_a_later_move_without_rotation_keeps_it`: `rotation: [0, 0, 2, 2]` comes back as `[0, 0, 0.7071…, 0.7071…]`, and the part's X and Y extents swap. A later move with no rotation keeps the turn.
- `move_model_refuses_by_name_and_a_refusal_enters_no_history`: each case is refused by name: a fixture, the work offset, an unknown name, a zero quaternion, a missing position, a 2-number position. None of them moves anything, and the next `undo` still undoes `add_fixture`.

title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

Changelog: grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic grblHAL 3-axis machine; G41/G42, G84, probing and go-home are refused by name

Fixes #710

title: fix(app): the program sim sweeps a tap at its thread's minor diameter
body:
**Replaces #271**, which closed itself on 2026-11-10 when its branch was pushed: the old fork `austin62jake/Camcraft` had left this repo's fork network, so GitHub could no longer follow its head. Same commits, now from the new fork `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, with `main` f42d3788 merged in (no conflicts). The review history and mkinney's conflict notes are on #271.

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, created 2026-11-10 from upstream `main` f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4).

**Partial fix for #266.** This removes one of the two checks that refuse a tap on a normally modelled hole. The other one still blocks the post; see "What is left" below.

### What changed

- The program sim (the stock-sim clause of the post gate) swept a Tap-kind tool at its full major diameter. CAD models a tapped hole at the thread's minor (tap-drill) size, and a tap only cuts the thread band outside that wall. So the sim read the band as a gouge down the whole hole wall and refused the post.
- A Tap-kind tool now sweeps its thread's core: `diameter / 2 - 0.5413 x pitch`. That is the ISO 724 radial thread depth, the same constant the thread-mill generator already uses (`machining2d::THREAD_DEPTH_PER_PITCH`). For M6 x 1 the core is Ø4.917.
- The rule lives in one place, `operation::tool_law::cutting_radius`, so a later fix to the generator's verify can read the same number. Every other tool still sweeps half its diameter. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name.
- A tap over a hole smaller than its core, or over solid metal, is still a gouge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-minor-sweep.md`.

### Readings

| Case (M6 x 1 tap, plate with a blind hole) | Program sim before | Program sim after |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | gouge, worst 12.000 mm on the hole wall | clean, 0 gouge cells |
| Ø3 hole (too small) | gouge | gouge (still refused) |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`: fails on `main` (`worst 12.000 mm at (-0.31, -2.94, z 8.0)`), passes with the fix.
- `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge`: guards the other side; passes before and after.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

**On this head (9410e5ba, `main` f42d3788 merged), Windows 10:**

- The quick gate's plan (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 4`): app lib 103 passed, plus 24 suites, 130 passed: `carried_fixtures_cache` 6, `carried_verify` 8, `contour_arc_sim` 1, `edge_break_bound` 3, `edge_break_gate` 5, `lathe_field_sim` 6, `lathe_field_tools` 2, `post_not_judged` 4, `posting` 17, `probe_only_sim` 2, `real_tip_contour` 4, `rotary_field_parity` 3, `setup_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `stock_engine_agreement` 0, `stock_export` 2, `stock_field_cost` 0, `stock_sim_document` 9, `stock_view` 4, `tap_sim` 2, `tool_law` 4, `verify` 21, `wall_column_gouge` 3. 7 are `#[ignore]`d in the source (`rotary_field_parity` 1, `stock_engine_agreement` 3, `stock_field_cost` 1, `verify` 2). No failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**On the earlier heads (#271):**


- Both pinning tests alone, with the fix, and with `stock_sim.rs` put back to `main` (the first one fails there as above).
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: app lib plus 13 suites (the gate map's `stock_sim` and `tool_law` suites plus `tap_sim`), 155 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The app, through `camcraft-cli mcp`, built from this branch (upstream `main` 897a820 plus this commit): imported a plate STL with a round Ø5 blind hole, added `TAP-M6` and a Drill/Tap op, generated, verified. The program gate now reports `ok` with no problems. With a Ø3 hole it still reports `gouge: program cuts below the model in 127 cell(s), worst 6.00 mm`.
- Baseline batch tier on clean `main` 897a820 on this machine: all suites pass except three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which also fail without this change. Not run on Linux or macOS.

### What is left (why this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`)

With this fix the Ø5 tap job still does not post. The op's own verify flags `move 1 cuts past the finish surface` and `move 2 cuts past the finish surface` (the tap feeding in and out). That verify hands one tool radius (`tool.geom()`) to every law, including the rapids laws, where a tap's full diameter is the right envelope: a tap must never rapid into the thread band. I tried shrinking only the containment solid law's cutter; the tangency law still flags the same two moves, so I dropped that. Fixing it means splitting the cutting radius from the rapid envelope in the verifier's inputs, and it meets the convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs` that a tapped hole is modelled at the tap's major diameter. I left that for you to decide on the issue.

title: feat(ui,app): every picker resolves through the one pick rule (#692 step 2)
body:
**Stacked on #705** (#692 step 1). It includes #705's commit until that merges; its own commit is the last one.

## What changed (step 2 of #692)
Every viewport picker and the MCP pick tools now resolve through #705's one pick rule. No page carries its own pick logic.

### The UI router: `crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs` (new)
- It builds the `PickRay` from the camera, in perspective or ortho.
- It converts the pixel radius to mm by depth.
- It says which kinds the armed tool accepts:

| Tool | Accepts |
|---|---|
| Plane row | faces only (#554) |
| Axis by edge | edges |
| Axis by two points | points |
| Operation geometry | Face, Edge (with the face between edges) or Vertex mode |
| Boundary | faces or edges |

- **Hover** uses exactly the rule its click would.
- **Origin/WCS chips** read the operation picks, so they get the same rule.

### Removed from the UI
- **`interact.rs`:** `pick_face`, `pick_edge`, `hover_feature_at`, `edge_nearest`, `point_seg_dist_px` and `feature_of_facet`. The old edge pick was screen-space, with no depth test, and offered facet seams. The file drops from 1779 to 1542 lines.
- **`vertex_pick.rs`:** its local nearest/sight logic. It drops from 271 to 122 lines.

### App side
- **`pick/feature_sel.rs` (new):** maps a pick to the `FeatureSel` the pages store (`Chain`, run or `Segment`). `check_pickable` refuses a pick by id that a click could never make.
- **MCP `list_features`:** now lists only feature-edge chains and feature points.
- **Graph cache:** cached per facet allocation, so hover never re-hashes a mesh.
- **Occlusion:** capped at 32 sight rays per candidate tier, a choice measured on `sample_ap214`.

### Intended behaviour changes (#692's rule)
- Rim vertices of round holes and bosses are no longer pickable points.
- Facet seams of smooth walls are no longer edges.
- Hidden edges are no longer pickable.
- In the feature modes, the stock-mesh hover triangle gives way to the feature highlight.

Thresholds and trade-offs are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-wire.md`.

## Tested
**New UI tests** (`egui_app::tests::one_pick_rule`, real egui_kittest clicks):
- `a_click_on_a_flat_faces_diagonal_picks_the_face_never_an_edge`

**New MCP test:** `mcp_pick::listed_chains_and_vertices_follow_the_one_pick_rule`.

**Existing tests rewritten to the new rule:** `vertex_pick_tests` (3, same claims through the real State), `law_tests::feature_pick_tests`, and one `plane_face_pick` assertion.

**Gate:**
- ui: all binaries green (lib 427).
- app: lib 103, `feature_pick` 7, `feature_pick_wire` 4, `pick` 9, `mcp_pick` 3, `mcp` 13, `vertex_pick` 4, `plane_align` 8, `plane_align_edges` 5, `axis_align` 10, `wcs_align` 5, `face_origin` 3, `feature` 18, `fixture_ux` 9, `probe_pick` 9, `mcp_setup` 4.

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one the origin stays the model's own. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - four kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

- The pin commit alone is red: at `35f399d1` the `wcs_roles` binary does not compile (no `pick::Role`/`align_roles` on main) and the ui lib does not compile (no `crate::wcs_pick`, row unwired) - the API and surface the pins demand did not exist.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` - 6 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` - 103 passed. Full `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (state.rs and interact.rs touched) - 430 passed, 5 ignored. Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` (`4827fde6`) and re-run green.
- Pre-existing on `origin/main`, untouched here: `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` does not compile - its `OpParams::Threading` initializer was never given #629's `hand` field (verified broken at both `dfb5e6a8` and `4827fde6`). It is the only build failure under `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run`; fixing it belongs in its own PR.

Changelog: the Setups page can set the WCS from feature picks - click faces, edges, corners and walls in the viewport, say what each one sets, and Apply places the work zero on the fitted frame, undo and redo included (#701)

Fixes #701

title: feat(app): one feature graph and pick API - welded faces, feature edges and points, visible-first (#692 step 1)
body:
## What changed (step 1 of #692)
This adds one app-layer picking service. Step 2 (a separate PR) moves every UI picker and the MCP pick tools onto it. No picker uses it yet, so app behaviour is unchanged.

### New modules
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_graph.rs` (330):** the feature graph of a mesh.
  - Welded faces are the existing `geometry::feature` patches, reused through `model::features_of_local`. `list_features` is unchanged.
  - Feature edges are creases between welded faces, plus open boundary edges. Seams between the strips of a tessellated wall are filtered out.
  - Feature points are corners (3 or more edges meet), turns over 30° and chain ends.
  - The graph has a cap-8 cache keyed by the facets' digest.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_arc.rs` (90):** circle and arc centres of round feature-edge runs.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_pick.rs` (314):** the one pick API, `pick_feature(world, &PickQuery { ray, radius, kinds, through }, skip)`, with `pick_bodies` for world-free callers.
  - It finds the front-most surface, then snaps point → centre → edge → face, only among the accepted kinds.
  - Edges and points must be visible from the eye: a perspective view checks the sight line, an ortho view the parallel view line. `through = true` turns the occlusion check off.
- **`pick.rs`:** registers the new modules; `ray_triangle` becomes `pub(crate)` so the new code shares it.

The thresholds and the alternatives dropped are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-graph.md`.

body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/671-plasma-post.md` (the sources and ten choices). CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md are updated.

...

## How tested
- **`plasma_post` (5):**
  - the inch and mm goldens, with structural checks: no Z/S/T/M3-M9/M6, per-contour order, G30 after every M205, ending `G30 M30`;
  - the in-app dump equals the `.cl` golden;
  - the control-comp golden;
  - a stream round-trip, plus malformed-record refusals;
  - an in-app 1300PL document posts through the gate.
- **`plasma_post_refusals` (5):** every refusal, the engine torch law, every milling builtin declining the stream, and the registry.
- **Pins updated:** plasma_machine, machine_library, plasma_profile, golden_cl and conformance.
- **Gate:**

title: feat(post): per-operation smoothing, opt-in, in every mill dialect
body:
## What changed

Requested by @spikeypineapple on #616. Smoothing differs per control, and the "auto" behaviour is maximum accuracy on finishing, with roughing aggressiveness following the stock left. The design was posted on the issue before code.

- **The option:** **"Smoothing per operation"**, a new document post option (`PostOptions.smoothing`), **off by default**.
  - **Off:** no smoothing PARAM is in the stream, so every program, and the `postOptions` object, is **byte-identical**.
  - **Saving:** the additive `smoothing` project key, absent when off. Undoable through `SetPostOptions`, and offered as a checkbox under the post picker for every mill post.
- **On, each operation states its ask** (`app::smoothing::of`) as `PARAM Smoothing <mm>` + `PARAM SmoothingMode finish|rough`:
  - **finish:** an op with a contour tolerance and no stock left asks **half** its tolerance (the control's deviation stacks on the verified path);
  - **rough:** an op leaving stock asks **stock × 0.2, capped at 0.25 mm, never more than that fifth** (no floor);
  - **nothing:** drilling, tapping, probing, threading, facing and the lathe kinds ask nothing.
- **Each mill post writes its control's words** after the section preamble and **undoes them at the section end**, so no tolerance leaks:

  | Post | On | Off |
  |---|---|---|
  | Tormach / LinuxCNC | `G64 P<tol>` | the header's `G64 P0.001` / `P0.025` |
  | Fanuc | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - G5.1 STATES NO TOLERANCE" (G5.1 has no tolerance word; review of #635) | none |
  | Haas | `G187 P3\|P1 E<tol>` | `G187` |
  | Siemens 840D | `CYCLE832(<tol>,_FINISH\|_ROUGH,1)` | `CYCLE832()` |
  | Heidenhain (ISO) | `G62 T<tol>` | `G62` |
  | Mazak | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - NO MAZAK FORM STATED" (no guessed word) | none |

- **Fanuc writes nothing yet:** `G5.1 Q1` states no tolerance, so it can't be held to the op's ask. A bounded form can follow with #614's Doosan sample. Decision record: `docs/decisions/616-smoothing.md`.

## How tested

title: fix(ui): orthographic depth maps into WebGPU's clip volume, not OpenGL's
body:
The ortho branch of `Camera::mvp` mapped depth the way OpenGL's `glOrtho` does - NDC z over [-1, +1]. WebGPU's clip volume wants `0 <= z <= w`, and the ortho matrix holds `clip.w == 1` (the #434 law tests pin that), so every point nearer than `(near + far) / 2` was clipped away before rasterization. With `far = 40 * dist`, that cut plane sits twenty times the orbit distance out: everything in view, so clicking **Orthographic** blanked the viewport.

Perspective carries the same OpenGL-style z row but `clip.w` is the eye distance there, which keeps clip z positive beyond ~0.2 mm - far closer than the camera can orbit - so perspective was unaffected.

## The change

The ortho z row (`viewport.rs`, the `[col][row]` proj literal) becomes

```rust
[0.0, 0.0, 1.0 / (near - far), 0.0],
[0.0, 0.0, near / (near - far), 1.0],
```

near maps to 0.0, far to 1.0, and ortho depth is now linear. The depth attachment already clears to 1.0 under `CompareFunction::Less`, so no pipeline or shader change is needed. The x/y rows already speak WebGPU and are untouched, as is the perspective branch (its z quirk costs depth precision, not geometry - out of scope here).

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::projection_tests::the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` - depth at the near plane, the far plane, and strictly between with monotonic climb. On main: "the near plane sits at -1".
- `gpu_render::orthographic_paints_the_band_perspective_does` - the stock box from `box_stock_paints_steel_over_background` under `test_cam()`, painted in both modes, with the same band bounds and a comparability check (each within 1.5x of the other). On main: 0/65536 pixels.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 378 passed, 5 ignored.
- `--test gpu_render`: 10 passed (9 existing + the new one).
- `--test trace_composite`: 4 passed (its first run hit the known pre-existing fallback-device crash race; clean on rerun, and it only exercises the untouched perspective path).

Changelog: orthographic view no longer blanks the viewport - the parallel depth row maps into WebGPU's clip volume (#600)

Fixes #600

title: feat(app): moving a part warns when it or its stock would sink into a fixture
body:
**Stacked on #576** (#571), which is on #566 (#561). It includes their commits until they merge.

## What changed
Locate (#561) already warns when the part or its stock would sink into a fixture. A plain Model-page move or turn didn't check at all (#582).
- **Shared check:** locate's sampled test and its by-name part and stock messages moved into a new `fixture_clash.rs`. `fixture_locate` calls it, and its wording is unchanged.
- **`MoveModel::new` now carries a `warning()`:**
  - the moved part is checked against every fixture in every setup, read through each setup's alignment;
  - a stock that follows the move is checked only in the setup that owns it;
  - setups with no fixtures are skipped without reading any geometry.
- **No double check in locate:** `MoveModel::locating` and the new `MoveFixture::locating` skip it, because locate runs its own check.
- **Fixture moves warn too:** `MoveFixture::new` checks the moved fixture against the setup's parts and stock.
- **Where it shows:** the status line reads `moved X - warning: …` (a shared `with_warning`), and MCP `move_fixture` gains a `"warning"` field.
- **A warning, not a refusal.** It warns on the result, so a part already inside a closed vise warns on every nudge.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/582-move-interpenetration.md`.

## How tested
- **New `move_interpenetration` (7):**
  - sinking into the floor warns by name;
  - a turn swinging into the jaw warns;
  - a stock-only sink warns for the stock alone;
  - a clear move warns nothing;
  - no fixtures means no check;
  - undo and redo of a warned move;

title: feat(app,ui): locate the part in a fixture (or the fixture on the part) by face/point mates
body:
Locates the part in an imported fixture, or the fixture on the part, by face and point mates (#561, part of #339). Branched from the fork's main (synced at v0.15.0) with upstream/main merged.

## What changed
**Solver:** `fixture_locate.rs`, with the pure solve in `fixture_locate_solve.rs`. It takes one to three mates in the fixture's setup frame: face–face, point–point, point-on-face and face-on-point. It returns one rigid transform and never touches the WCS.
- **Order:** 3-2-1 fixturing. The first face mate opposes the normals by the shortest turn. The second turns the part about that normal. A third must already agree. Then each mate fixes the remaining free motion, in mate order.
- **Nudge:** after the mates, a turn about the first fixture normal, then an X/Y/Z shift.
- **Pick reader:** `pick/mate.rs` reuses `outward_normal` and `facets_centroid` (#187/#330).

**Commands** (`commands/locate.rs`):
- `LocatePart` moves the part through `MoveModel`, so the stock follows. In a turned setup (#326) it composes into `AlignPartToSetup` instead.
- `LocateFixture` moves the fixture by the inverse, through `MoveFixture`.
- `Locate` wraps both for the UI and MCP. Every locate is one undo step.

**Refused by name at creation:**
- **Bodies:** no fixture, the machine table, a model that isn't a fixture, no part, or a pick on the wrong body.
- **Picks:** an edge or curved face, a zero-area face, or two mates on the same point or face.
- **Solve:** faces that can't oppose, contradicting mates, zero mates or more than three, a non-finite nudge, or "nothing would move".

**Interpenetration warns rather than refuses.** A sampled inside test (the fixture mesh's ray law) names the part, the fixture and a point.

**UI:**
- **Fixtures page:** a **Locate part…** verb on each row.
- **Model page:** a locate row.
- **Form:** Move the part / Move the fixture, Offset X/Y/Z, Turn, **Apply locate** (greyed with the solve's reason) and Remove last.
- **Picks:** part first, then fixture, routed through the existing face and vertex picking.

**MCP:** a `locate_part` tool. `list_features` accepts a fixture.

## Choices that differ from the issue (decision file: `docs/decisions/561-locate-part-fixture.md`)
- **A moved fixture doesn't mark the setup's ops stale.** That keeps the existing rule that workholding never stales a toolpath. The collision check re-judges live instead, and a test pins it. Moving the part does mark them stale, and undo clears it.
- **Maintainer's call: in an unaligned setup the part moves through `MoveModel`.** That changes its document placement, so in a multi-setup document it also moves the part in the other setups, and their ops go stale and need regenerating. A translation-only setup alignment was avoided, because it would make the setup count as aligned and refuse every non-2D op. An alternative is to refuse a locate in an unaligned multi-setup document and point to aligning the setup first.
- **Deferred:** point-pair mates don't turn the part (only face mates orient it); there's no preview before Apply; per-setup part placement for unaligned multi-setup documents.

## How tested
- **App `fixture_locate` (11):**
  - a face mate makes the faces coplanar with opposed normals;
  - floor, jaw and stop give a full location;
  - the offset and turn are exact;
  - LocateFixture moves the fixture, not the part;
  - undo and redo;
  - point mates;
  - degenerate and conflicting picks are refused by name;
  - the interpenetration warning;
  - ops go stale and undo clears it;
  - a moved fixture is re-judged live while the path stays fresh;
  - the turned-setup case.
- **MCP:** `mcp_setup::locate_part_seats_the_part_on_the_fixture_by_feature_ids`.
- **UI:**
  - `locate_tests`: apply a locate from the Fixtures page, with undo and redo; the Model page moves the fixture to the part;
  - `fixture_rows`: the locate tools fit inside the pane on both pages;
  - `structural.rs`: no locate draft is armed by default.
- **Regressions:** `fixtures`, `fixture_ux`, `fixture_mesh`, `fixture_mesh_posed`, `setup_align`, `plane_align`, `commands_undo`, `project_roundtrip`, `mcp`, `mcp_setup` and `mcp_pick` all pass. ui lib passes 379 of 380; the failure is the headless-GPU test, which needs a graphics adapter this machine doesn't have. Clippy (app and ui, `-D warnings`) is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
A GUI hands-on check (the picks in the viewport). That will be driven headless next.

title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body:
Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
- **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before.
- **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name:
  - a number outside 1-9999;
  - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`.

  Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time.
- **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves.
- **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool.
- **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead.
- **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set.

**Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals.
- **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `(<comment or machine name>)`.
- **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set.
- **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment.
- **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `%<name> G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name.
- **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N_<NAME>_MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`.

## How tested
- **New `program_info` tests (9):**
  - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set;
  - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone;
  - post-time refusals;
  - command validation, undo and redo;
  - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`);
  - per-op numbering;
  - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001;
  - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused.
- **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal).
- **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.**

## Not exercised
A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set.

Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258)
